| **Connie shared the following statement: **

_“I am Connie Buske, Medina County Precinct Chair 1D. I am a Texan by birth who has come to love conservative values and our constitution. I look for others who uphold these values and have found an outstanding woman who does just that. I would like to announce my endorsement for Julie Clark who is running for Congress in District 23. District 23 has 29 counties and spans from San Antonio to Del Rio and El Paso. Julie is by far the best candidate for the job and is a strong voice for all Americans.”_

_**I am deeply honored to have Connie’s endorsement**_ , and I’m grateful to have volunteered in the grassroots trenches with her in fighting for our shared values. The beauty of our Constitutional Republic is that we are invited to the table to make sure that what we stand for is represented in the work that responsive leaders accomplish in their commitment to serve us.

For too long, elected officials like Rep. Tony Gonzales have failed to deliver on promises that are matters of importance that We The People have volunteered, donated, and rallied for leaders to uphold.

It is our job as Americans to apply the Constitutional guidance we are charged with as citizens when our leaders fail to serve as responsive public servants. That’s why I saw it as my responsibility to see that Rep. Tony Gonzales was censured for his betrayal of our Republican values, and I am now seeking to unseat him so that Texans will have a leader who will keep their word and serve their best interests over foreign invaders!

**Peter, I look forward to serving you, Connie Buske and every other Texan who wants to see our borders secure, the rule of law upheld, and leaders who are accountable to the people.** [**Your support is absolutely critical for me to succeed in gaining the victory over Tony Gonzales. Can I count on you to chip in $23.00 today to symbolize our determination to triumph for the 23rd Congressional District?**](https://mcshanellc.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fcc3d4d56d2b95c7d6dfed110&id=3f4f0328e5&e=c982eb7ad4)

body:
Ken Calvert outed Mark Takano as gay against his will!

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/68818155/424229602/-1632984841?amount=3&refcode=MTFC_20230828_EMSPL_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NDZkMjMxOS1mYTQ1LWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rIG6llmKaxpk2AKOKh5V4V1qVhvbCaX_BLxJyzboYwI=) Hey, Peter. | | Today marks the 60th anniversary of the March on Washington, at which Martin Luther King, Jr. gave his "I Have a Dream" speech. It is a day to reflect upon the profound legacy of those who marched for civil rights, equality, and justice. It is a moment to reflect on our journey towards a more just and equitable society and to recognize the challenges we continue to face. The threats against voting rights nationwide, the recent striking down of affirmative action in college admissions, and the erosion of abortion rights by the Supreme Court serve as stark reminders that the fight for equality and justice is far from over. These actions undermine the principles of equity and opportunity that the civil rights movement sought to advance. Furthermore, we cannot ignore the growing threats of political violence and hatred against people of color, Jews, and LGBTQ+ individuals. We saw this again just this past weekend in Jacksonville. The rise of extremism and discrimination is a grave concern that demands immediate attention and action. While this must be a priority for every American, I want to underscore that this issue holds deep personal significance for me. My wife is Persian, and we have mixed-race children. Despite my privileges, this personal experience has provided me with important insight into the challenges and disparities that persist in our society. It only strengthens my commitment to the cause of racial justice and equity. On this historic anniversary, let us commit ourselves to the principles of justice, equality, and unity that have always defined the American spirit. Together, we can honor the legacy of those who marched before us by continuing the fight for a more equitable and inclusive future for all. _Conor_ |

clean_body: | | | | Today marks the 60th anniversary of the March on Washington, at which Martin Luther King, Jr. gave his "I Have a Dream" speech. It is a day to reflect upon the profound legacy of those who marched for civil rights, equality, and justice. It is a moment to reflect on our journey towards a more just and equitable society and to recognize the challenges we continue to face. The threats against voting rights nationwide, the recent striking down of affirmative action in college admissions, and the erosion of abortion rights by the Supreme Court serve as stark reminders that the fight for equality and justice is far from over. These actions undermine the principles of equity and opportunity that the civil rights movement sought to advance. Furthermore, we cannot ignore the growing threats of political violence and hatred against people of color, Jews, and LGBTQ+ individuals. We saw this again just this past weekend in Jacksonville. The rise of extremism and discrimination is a grave concern that demands immediate attention and action. While this must be a priority for every American, I want to underscore that this issue holds deep personal significance for me. My wife is Persian, and we have mixed-race children. Despite my privileges, this personal experience has provided me with important insight into the challenges and disparities that persist in our society. It only strengthens my commitment to the cause of racial justice and equity. On this historic anniversary, let us commit ourselves to the principles of justice, equality, and unity that have always defined the American spirit. Together, we can honor the legacy of those who marched before us by continuing the fight for a more equitable and inclusive future for all.
